Breakfast at the hotel. Then join a three-hour group city tour with an English-speaking guide.

Explore Argentina's capital and discover centuries of culture through its history, art and architecture. Its elegant buildings invite comparisons with Paris, while its museums, galleries, theatres and landmarks give the city a character of its own. Highlights include the old neighbourhood of La Boca and historic San Telmo, with bars, restaurants and the antiques market in Plaza Dorrego. At the heart of the city lies Plaza de Mayo, home to the Casa Rosada, the pink presidential palace associated with Evita Perón. The city is also known for its 67-metre Obelisk, erected to commemorate the proclamation of Argentina's independence. You'll visit elegant Recoleta, with its famous cemetery, the colonial-style Church of El Pilar and the nearby cultural and shopping centre. The tour also takes in modern Puerto Madero, Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park.

In the evening, enjoy a tango show with dinner. Tango is known around the world, and Argentina is where it took shape. On stage, the dancers bring its passion, skill and grace to life.

The dance grew up around the city's docks among poor immigrants, gauchos and others on the margins. Early tango was a more uninhibited dance performed by two men, and its name has been linked to the Latin tangere, meaning ‘to touch’. Over time, tango slowed and became more intimate. Orchestras began playing it, and the dance quickly grew in popularity. Tango remains one of the most sensual dances in the world, bringing together sincerity, gallantry and tenderness. The restaurant's décor sets the mood, while several traditional dishes and fine Argentine wines round off the evening.

Transfer to the port early in the morning and take the ferry to Montevideo for a tour with an English-speaking guide. After some free time, return to Buenos Aires and transfer to your hotel. Ferry tickets are included.
